framework.reasoning: PyTorch is the de-facto standard for NeRF/diffusion-adjacent research (default per planning rules since the paper never names a framework). CUDA is marked optional/not required because this environment has no GPU and no access to Stable Diffusion / CLIP / DINO checkpoint hosts (not on the egress allowlist); the repo runs CPU-only against a synthetic toy scene by default but is written to transparently accelerate on CUDA if available. HuggingFace integration is intentionally NOT wired in as a hard dependency because the real inpainting/language-field models it would pull in are unreachable in this sandbox -- see risk_assessment. YAML is sufficient given the modest config surface; Hydra/OmegaConf would be overkill for a single-paper repro.

tensor_flows.name: Base NeRF forward + volumetric rendering
steps: out = JointNeRFField(enc, view_dirs)                             -> density [N_rays,n_samples,1], rgb [N_rays,n_samples,3], lang [N_rays,n_samples,d_l]

tensor_flows.name: Object removal via neural field resampling
steps: hits = RayBoxExcluder.intersect(rays_o, rays_d, b)                     -> [N,2] (t_enter,t_exit) or NaN
intervals = build_exclusion_intervals(near, far, hits)                -> per-ray list of valid t-segments (near-seg, far-seg)
t_uniform = TwoStageResampler.uniform_resample(intervals, n_uniform)  -> [N, n_uniform], none inside b
t_hier = TwoStageResampler.hierarchical_resample(intervals, weights, n_hierarchical) -> [N, n_hierarchical], none inside b

tensor_flows.name: Region-wise teacher-student distillation (Eq. 6) + language field update

output.name: F_hat_Theta (student), L' (updated language field)
output.shape: trained student NeRF params + language field params

steps: S_prime = RegionCompositor.compose(points, F_Theta, F_tilde_Theta, box, motion)  -> per-region supervision tensors {outside_box: F_Theta, inside_removal_box: F_tilde_Theta, relocated_object_region: F_Theta(under motion)}
phase1: student = StudentDistiller.distill(...,n_steps_phase1) using field-level L_distill term (density/color along rays)
phase2: student = StudentDistiller.distill(...,n_steps_phase2) adding image-level RGB+depth L_distill term
L_prime = LanguageFieldUpdater.update(student, original_poses, n_iterations)     -> supervised by CLIP/DINO-substitute features rendered from fixed student

risk_assessment.description: The NEO-Dataset benchmark (12 registered pre/post-edit tabletop scenes) is referenced as forthcoming/project-page-hosted but is not bundled with the paper and was not fetchable in this offline sandbox. All quantitative results in this repro are computed on a procedurally generated synthetic toy scene, NOT the real NEO-Dataset.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Built a self-contained ToySceneGenerator producing analogous pre/post-edit multi-view RGB-D scans with known ground truth, so the full pipeline and metric code are exercised and testable end-to-end; results are clearly labeled synthetic in the comparison report.

risk_assessment.description: The real inpainting backend (Stable Diffusion, per Fig. 6 caption) and the real language field backbone (CLIP + DINO) require downloading large pretrained checkpoints from hosts not on this environment's network allowlist.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implemented a pluggable InpaintingBackend interface with a working OpenCV heuristic-fill default, and a pluggable language-embedding interface with a fixed deterministic hash-based embedding default. Both are one line swaps for real diffusers/CLIP/DINO models on a machine with internet + GPU access. This is the single biggest fidelity gap versus the paper and is called out explicitly in the reproducibility score.

risk_assessment.description: Base NeRF backbone architecture (hash-grid vs plain MLP), all training hyperparameters (optimizer, LR, batch size, step counts), and the loss weights lambda_rec/lambda_reg are never stated numerically in the paper (SIR training_pipeline confidence 0.45).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Used a plain positional-encoding MLP (simplest faithful choice) and standard NeRF-literature defaults (Adam, 5e-4 LR, 1024 rays/batch, equal loss weights), all flagged '# ASSUMED' in config.yaml with the SIR confidence noted, and exposed as config fields so they are trivially swept/tuned.

risk_assessment.description: AnyGrasp (external grasp-planning dependency) is a proprietary/licensed system and not reproducible here.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implemented AnyGraspStub with an interface-compatible but explicitly non-faithful placeholder (simple top-down/side candidate generation at the bbox surface) so downstream pipeline code has a real call site to integrate against; never claimed as a reproduction of AnyGrasp's grasp quality.

risk_assessment.description: Exact virtual-viewpoint count for the inpainting hemisphere augmentation and the re-render interval n are unspecified (ambiguities #2 and #4).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Exposed n_virtual_views and reinpaint_interval_n as config fields with documented assumptions; ablation harness can vary them directly.

risk_assessment.description: Numerical instability risk in the two-stage ray resampling when a ray's box intersection interval spans almost the entire ray (near-degenerate remaining intervals), potentially producing NaNs in the PDF-based hierarchical resample.
risk_assessment.mitigation: RayBoxExcluder.intersect clamps degenerate intervals and TwoStageResampler falls back to uniform sampling over the full ray when the valid-interval union is below a minimum length threshold; covered by a unit test.
